idiom_name: typed sequence envelope (SequenceId / position / size) with Map<SequenceId, Part[]>
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds a contract to the JavaScript realization: model the three fields as an explicit envelope type and validate it at the consumer boundary, then feed the same Map-based reassembly behind KafkaJS or amqplib. The types make position arithmetic and the release condition checkable at compile time, but they order nothing and complete nothing - the transport provides the ordering it provides, and the receiver still owns the buffer, the gap check and the expiry.
pitfalls: Header values arrive as unknown from the wire: parse and range-check pos and size (1-based, size at least 1) instead of casting the envelope into existence.
A map keyed by seqId alone collides across producers; include the producer or a UUID in the key.
Array(size).fill(undefined) hides a duplicate position that overwrote a part; a seen-set distinguishes duplicates from gaps.
